derived_observations: Temporal stacking as a binary pattern is not a separator: both sides have near and far maturity opportunities coexisting on 11 of 12 observed days, productive spend on all 12 days, and SELL on all 12 days.
Nearly all SELL cash on both sides occurs while far maturity is already in flight (self 99.4%, opponent 100%).
The large separator is stack depth and economic wave size: opponent carries substantially more far-maturity assets and performs much more productive spending while future maturity is in flight.
Across Day0-11, opponent realized 27262.6 SELL cash vs self 19797.5, retained 18861.0 surplus after operating vs self 5737.7, and made 15182.6 productive spend vs self 7182.9.
The gap becomes especially large by Day10: far-maturity assets are 34.8 vs 10.5, actual production 30.4 vs 10.6, surplus 5904.4 vs 708.1, and productive spend 3861.6 vs 947.0.

Therefore the world does not support a simple rule 'have overlapping maturities'; both already do. The unresolved question is what transitions build and sustain a deeper future-maturity stack while producing enough surplus to fund the next wave.
boundary: No Candidate, Direction, pressure variable, or policy mutation was introduced.
Near maturity means a public-rule next-output opportunity within 0-2 days; far maturity means 3+ days.
Maturity is an opportunity, not guaranteed realization or profit.
SELL and productive spend are not causally linked by cash lineage.
No composite temporal-stack score is adopted.
